Medieval History.Rajput Kingdoms:
INTRODUCTION
After the decline of Harsha Empire in the 7th century CE, north India witnessed the emergence of several regional kingdoms known as Rajput states. This period is marked by political fragmentation and rise of warrior clans.

ORIGIN OF RAJPUTS
• Various theories exist regarding origin
• Agnikula theory mentions origin from fire ritual at Mount Abu
• Some historians link them to foreign tribes like Hunas
• Others consider them as descendants of ancient Kshatriyas

MAJOR RAJPUT CLANS
• Chauhans ruled Ajmer and Delhi
• Solankis or Chalukyas ruled Gujarat
• Paramaras ruled Malwa
• Chandellas ruled Bundelkhand
• Gahadavalas ruled Kannauj

POLITICAL STRUCTURE
• Feudal system dominated polity
• King was supreme but depended on samantas feudatories
• Samantas provided military support and governed local regions
• Frequent conflicts among Rajput states weakened unity

ADMINISTRATION
• Decentralized administration with local autonomy
• Land grants to Brahmanas and officials were common
• Village administration played important role

ECONOMY
• Agriculture was main occupation
• Land revenue was main source of income
• Trade declined compared to ancient period but local trade continued

SOCIETY
• Society was hierarchical based on caste system
• Rajputs followed warrior code of honor
• Practices like Jauhar and Sati were prevalent
• Women had limited role in public life

MILITARY
• Strong emphasis on valor and personal bravery
• Lack of strategic unity among kingdoms
• Cavalry and infantry formed main army

ART AND ARCHITECTURE
• Development of temple architecture in Nagara style
• Famous temples include Khajuraho by Chandellas
• Forts and palaces were built for defense

SIGNIFICANCE
Rajput period represents transition to medieval polity with feudal structure. It also contributed to development of regional cultures and architecture.

IMPORTANT POINTS
• Emerged after decline of Harsha
• Feudal polity with samanta system
• Major clans Chauhans, Solankis, Paramaras
• Known for valor but lacked unity
• Temple architecture flourished

PYQ TRAP
UPSC often asks about Rajput polity. It was feudal with strong role of samantas, not centralized like Mauryas.
